JAMES1974.title: David John James (1974), A Cytochemical and Biochemical Study of Acid Hydrolases in Developing Plant Cells
JAMES1974.access: full extracted PDF text; PDF screenshot not available (cache miss)
JAMES1974.scope: Cultivar Cambridge Vigour; IV.1 growth stages 1969, IV.3 microscopy measurements 1972; 10 cell observations per developmental stage in IV.3
JAMES1974.access_caveat: Use printed page numbers. IV.1 selection sizes A/B are nominal criteria, NOT means. IV.3 D/E missing.

ARIZA2011.title: Ariza et al. (2011), Fruit misshapen in strawberry cultivars is related to achenes functionality, Annals of Applied Biology 158, 130–138
ARIZA2011.type: Research article; full text of original article indexed via ResearchGate
ARIZA2011.access: original published table in accessible article text (ResearchGate mirror), not publisher original PDF
ARIZA2011.scope: Field-grown Camarosa, Medina, Ventana; well-formed (WF) vs misshapen (MF); means ±SE of n=3 plot averages; 50 fruits/plot for size, 30 fruits/plot for achene size/class counts
ARIZA2011.access_caveat: Big achenes defined >0.6 mm; small <0.4 mm; intermediate sizes not included in big/small counts. Table 2 number of total achenes need not equal sum of these classes.

CURRIE1997.title: Michael Brian Currie (1997), Source-Sink Relations in Kiwifruit, PhD thesis, Massey University
CURRIE1997.access: full extracted PDF text; PDF screenshot not available (cache miss)
CURRIE1997.scope: Chapter 3 girdling experiment on green-fleshed A. deliciosa (cultivar not stated for this specific table in the extracted methods; Hayward is common in the study but not guaranteed for these rows), harvested 150 days after full bloom for 3.4 and 3.5, leaf:fruit ratios 1 vs 4, girdling at day 7/28/56. Marginal means (PMM) due to missing data.
CURRIE1997.access_caveat: Table 3.4 diameter along Dmax/Dmin transects, not isotropic cell diameter. Table 3.5 counts are per straight radial transect, not total fruit counts. Thesis copyright: private study only, reproduce factual numerical observations but not original images/chapters.

JEON2024.title: Jeon, Oh & Song (2024), Response of Fruit Growth and Quality to the Spray of Plant Growth Regulator in Yellow-fleshed Kiwifruits, Horticultural Science & Technology 42, 234–246
JEON2024.type: Primary research article; publisher full HTML
JEON2024.access: full publisher HTML tables and methods
JEON2024.scope: Yellow-fleshed Sweet Gold and Jecy Gold grown in Jeju; Control/one/two/three sprays of Benefits PZ starting after bloom; cell samples ~1.2×1.2 mm, 10 samples each treatment, per authors methods; tissue widths n=3, cells n=10, mean ±SE.
JEON2024.access_caveat: Table 3 widths are total measured radial components, not whole-fruit diameter; totals 21–25 mm for one side. Table 4 cell counts in samples, not number of all cells in fruit.

limitations: Exact PDF screenshots of James and Currie failed due to cache miss; all PDF numbers were checked in parsed full text, but not directly against page bitmaps.
ARIZA2011 original journal Table 2 was read from hosted full-text copy rather than publisher rendering.
CURRIE1997 Chapter 3 cultivar not independently attested by nearby methods in parsed text: cultivar_unverified_ch3 is intentional; do not assign Hayward without confirmation.
JEON2024 is A. chinensis var. chinensis, not green Hayward A. deliciosa; spray treatments are not baseline controls.
Counts within sampled area or radial transect must never be treated as total cells of the fruit.
No reliable fruit vascular diameter, exact strawberry cuticle thickness in a primary table, or region-resolved strawberry ripe-cell table extracted here; leave model parameters uncalibrated.
No direct transfer of historical embryological stage means or treated experimental fruit measurements into a universal cultivar preset.
